title: C. HEAT AND TEMPERATURE — Q61–90 (part 1)
source: Physics MCQ Test OPTIMIZED — C. HEAT AND TEMPERATURE — Q61–90, pages 3-3 [Physics_MCQ_Test_OPTIMIZED.md]
textbookText: 61. Heat is best defined as: A) Energy in transit between two bodies due to temperature difference B) A substance contained within a body C) The degree of hotness of a body D) A property measured directly with a thermometer only

62. Temperature is best defined as: A) The degree of hotness or coldness of a body, related to average kinetic energy of molecules B) The total heat energy contained in a body C) The amount of work a body can do D) A form of stored chemical energy

63. On the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales, the ice point and steam point are respectively: A) 0°C, 100°C and 32°F, 212°F B) 0°C, 100°C and 0°F, 100°F C) 32°C, 212°C and 0°F, 100°F D) 100°C, 0°C and 212°F, 32°F
64. The relation between Celsius (C) and Fahrenheit (F) scales is: A) C/5 = (F−32)/9 B) C/9 = (F−32)/5 C) C = F − 32 D) F/5 = C/9
65. Absolute zero on the Kelvin scale corresponds to: A) −273.15°C, the temperature at which molecular kinetic energy is theoretically minimum B) 0°C, the ice point C) −100°C D) 273.15°C

66. A constant-volume gas thermometer measures temperature based on: A) Change in pressure of a fixed volume of gas with temperature B) Change in length of a mercury column C) Change in electrical resistance of a metal wire D) Expansion of a bimetallic strip

67. Thermal equilibrium between two bodies in contact means: A) They have reached the same temperature and no net heat flows between them B) They have the same mass C) They have the same specific heat capacity D) One body has completely transferred all its heat to the other

68. The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics is the basis for: A) The concept and measurement of temperature using a thermometer B) The first law of energy conservation C) The concept of entropy D) Newton's law of cooling

69. A platinum resistance thermometer works on the principle that: A) Electrical resistance of platinum varies systematically with temperature B) Platinum expands more than mercury per degree C) Platinum changes color at high temperature D) Platinum has zero resistance at all temperatures

70. Which thermometer is most suitable for measuring very high temperatures (like furnace temperatures) without contact? A) Pyrometer (radiation thermometer) B) Mercury-in-glass thermometer C) Alcohol thermometer D) Clinical thermometer

71. Why is mercury preferred over water in liquid-in-glass thermometers? A) Mercury does not wet glass, expands uniformly, and has a wide liquid range B) Mercury is cheaper than water C) Water has a higher boiling point than mercury D) Mercury is transparent while water is not
72. The triple point of water (used to define the Kelvin scale) occurs at: A) 273.16 K, where ice, water, and vapor coexist in equilibrium B) 373 K C) 0 K D) 100°C exactly

73. A clinical thermometer has a kink (constriction) near the bulb to: A) Prevent mercury from flowing back until deliberately shaken down B) Increase the sensitivity of the thermometer C) Allow it to measure much higher temperatures than normal D) Make the thermometer cheaper to manufacture
74. Normal human body temperature is approximately: A) 37°C (98.6°F) B) 100°C C) 25°C D) 45°C

75. Which of these is an extraordinary fact about the Kelvin scale? A) It has no negative values because it starts from absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature B) It uses the same zero point as the Celsius scale C) It is only used for gas temperatures, never solids D) One kelvin is twice as large as one degree Celsius

76. A thermocouple thermometer measures temperature by: A) The emf (Seebeck effect) generated at the junction of two dissimilar metals B) The expansion of a metal rod C) The pressure change in a sealed gas D) The color change of a liquid crystal
77. -40 is the unique temperature where: A) Celsius and Fahrenheit scales give the same numerical reading (−40°C = −40°F) B) Water boils C) Water freezes D) Kelvin scale reads zero

78. The range of a clinical thermometer is typically: A) About 35°C to 42°C, suited for human body temperature range B) 0°C to 100°C, the full range of water's liquid state C) −200°C to 200°C D) 0 K to 273 K

79. Which property makes a substance suitable as a "thermometric property" (e.g., resistance, emf, length, pressure)? A) It must vary continuously, uniquely, and measurably with temperature B) It must remain constant regardless of temperature C) It must be visible to the naked eye only D) It must be a solid at room temperature

80. Two thermometers, mercury and alcohol, may show a slight discrepancy in reading between the fixed points because: A) Different liquids expand non-uniformly (non-linearly) with temperature in slightly different ways B) One thermometer measures heat, the other measures temperature C) Alcohol thermometers cannot be calibrated at all D) Mercury only works above 100°C
